evidence: independent audit4 of numerical, uncalibrated simulations; not physical verification

checks.finding: windEstimate() seeds its ±1 m/s bias from the case seed, so the 48-case grid samples only 3 bias draws per wind. leapfrog keMax and C0 range pass on seeds 11–13 but fail on seeds 14–22 (tail5.5_s15 15.03 J / 54.9 m; tail6_s17 16.05 J; tail5.5_s20 15.49 J; tail6_s21 50.5 m). towglider passes all 48 but crossL7.5_s11 (off-grid, gate on) gives headClear 0.934 m. kite2 KE margin 0.62 J. Grid-only safety maxima are not robust.
checks.action: integrator: judge safety maxima (keMax, headClear, range) on ≥6 seeds and an off-grid band, or decouple the bias seed from the turbulence seed

checks.metric: idealised estimators still in judged runs (rule 5)
checks.finding: All launch/park gates use windEstimate() (compliant for all three). But: leapfrog tracker latency compensation and GNSS feed-forward use the true LOS increment/rate (+noise, 50 Hz) and guidance uses true rider state; towglider camera mount is pointed from the true rider position; kite2 window controller uses noise-free kite position/velocity and true dynamic pressure. Effects measured: leapfrog jitter 1.64 → 2.01 (est. comp, 5 Hz GNSS) → 3.43 (1 Hz GNSS, avail 64.6 %); towglider 2.45 → 2.56–2.81 with 3–5 % detection noise; kite2 doubled noise avail +1 pp, KE 14.31 J.
checks.favours: leapfrog (jitter/avail rest on the rider-tag link rate)
checks.action: integrator: add a shared rider-tag/tracker estimator (GNSS rate, latency, noise) in common/ and require it for all pointing/guidance

checks.finding: Shared artefactCounts(≥2 px) is applied, but each concept projects its own parts. towglider tests the leash only at polyline vertices (misses the near-camera segment 3–13 px) and omits the 3 mm wand (−1.4 pp own test, −6.7 pp if the subject box includes skis). kite2 boom 1.66 px median meets the rule only because it is 3 mm (structurally infeasible, A4-K2-01). "Bounding box" of the subject is not defined (body vs incl. skis).
checks.action: integrator: provide a shared segment/cylinder projector and define the subject box (bodyPoints feet/head/shoulders)

checks.metric: worn rigid members excluded from headClear
checks.finding: kite2 passive boom (free pivot, moves with the line) 0.33 m from the helmet centre; towglider wand 1.165 m (included would pass). Exclusion of a free-pivoting boom as "worn rigid" is generous; with a buildable 1.2 m boom kite2 headClear 0.84 m.
checks.action: integrator: count free-pivoting members as airborne parts

checks.finding: leapfrog sensitivity figures relayed in the round-4 report (mass +10 % → 69.7 %, bias ±2 → 17.65 J, stow 13.5 s → 33.1 s) are not in dev/leapfrog/results.json (18-case subset: 65.6 %, 17.92 J, 33.4 s); auditor full-48: 67.7 %, 17.92 J, 33.2 s. Same direction, all fail.
checks.action: developers: report only numbers traceable to results.json

checks.finding: All three packVol values are assumed envelopes (no CAD/fold measurement); kite2 kept the round-3 2.86 L constant despite a larger winch and 6-section boom; towglider wand 8 g missing from mass; leapfrog morph mechanism budgeted at micro-servo scale (LisHawk uses 3×7.1 g servos at 284 g).
checks.action: mock-up pack and weigh before any further ranking on these metrics

checks.finding: common/ unchanged since the dev runs (kite2 commonHash 5d71ed4a96c0 and towglider fileHashes match the live files). All three reproduce on a copy (kite2 within 0.05 pp, leapfrog and towglider exactly). Concept tests pass on the copy (kite2 21, leapfrog 24, towglider 18).
